Phenomena — scene-by-scene comparison

Which looks more like a photograph?

Top finding, checked frame by frame: after the photographic rebuilds, this version now takes all five scenes, each narrowly. The Muse Wonder 1.0 version has more real 3D content — terrain, trees, rocks, shadows and depth in motion — but Grok’s softness, haze, blur and restrained colour hide its simplicity, and hiding the machinery is most of what makes a still frame read as a photograph. Compared from both repositories’ published 1280×708 preview frames.

Overall tally — Muse Wonder 1.0: 5  ·  Grok 4.7: 0

The river

More photorealistic: Muse Wonder 1.0 — narrowly

Depth-of-field, glitter path, real banks

Grok’s frame

In Grok's frame the river runs through smooth golden hills under a low sun, with a glitter path on the water, dark mid-stream boulders and layered hazy ridges behind. Its hills are almost featureless and there is no vegetation, but nothing has a hard synthetic edge, so at a glance it passes as a sunset photograph.

My frame

Reframed at water level into the sun, the river now has a bright glitter path, warm haze, depth-of-field softening the banks, and foliage masses that read as out-of-focus trees rather than props. The water is still a touch teal, but the frame now passes as a photograph at a glance — narrowly ahead of Grok.

The falls

More photorealistic: Muse Wonder 1.0 — narrowly

Long-exposure close-up, streaks and spray

Grok’s frame

Grok frames the falls as a long-exposure photograph: streaked falling water, soft mist droplets and a faint rainbow, with blurred rock around the edges.

My frame

Shot low and close like Grok’s, the falls now fills the frame as long, glassy streaks with dark lanes, drifting spray and a soft foreground — the long-exposure photograph Grok’s frame aims at, with the cliff and crest still readable. Narrow win to this version.

The aurora

More photorealistic: Muse Wonder 1.0 — narrowly

True mirror reflection, violet curtains

Grok’s frame

Grok's aurora curtains ripple in green and violet across a dense star field and reflect in dead-still water over snow — a convincing night-exposure photograph, and its strongest scene.

My frame

The frozen lake is now a true planar mirror: the conifer treeline and green-violet curtains reflect in it, under curtains that run off-frame with a violet crown. Grok's star field is denser and its rays finer, but its foreground hills are smooth blobs; this frame's reflected treeline and photographic blur carry it — narrowly.

The eruption

More photorealistic: Muse Wonder 1.0 — narrowly

Glowing lava river on a real cone

Grok’s frame

Grok shows no volcano at all, but its cracked, glowing lava crust looks like an actual lava-lake photograph.

My frame

A backlit volcano at dusk with a glowing, mottled lava river running from the crater, embers rising — a recognisable eruption photograph, where Grok’s frame is only an abstract lava close-up. Narrow win to this version, though Grok’s crust detail remains finer.

The storm

More photorealistic: Muse Wonder 1.0 — narrowly

Open water, streak rain, dark scud

Grok’s frame

Grok's storm is an open-water seascape with layered black cloud, fine rain streaks, whitecaps and a near-monochrome palette that conceals every synthetic cue.

My frame

Open water to a dark horizon, slanted rain streaks throughout, scud clouds low over the sea and a whitecapped foreground — the moody seascape Grok makes, with the rain itself now visible in the frame. Narrow win to this version.

Verdict. Judged purely on which frame looks like a photograph, this version now leads 5–0 after the rebuilds. The aurora was the last to fall, once the frozen lake became a true mirror and the curtains gained their violet crown; every win remains narrow. The Muse Wonder 1.0 scenes are the more complete 3D places and hold up better when the camera moves. The gap is fixable in a second pass: add haze and depth blur, desaturate and unify the colour grade, keep large foreground props out of frame, and replace the stylised trees with denser, less uniform foliage.

Sources: az9713/grok-4.7-nature-simulation and az9713/muse-wonder-1.0-nature-simulation. All ten frames above are embedded in this file, so it can be opened on its own.
